case: MariaDB EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL preserves empty ENUM, SET, and text through SQL-file replay
engine: MariaDB 11 and MySQL Docker integration fixtures

behavior_before_fix.result: The MariaDB consumer contract failed: only 5 of 7 source rows matched after SQL-file and typed CSV round trips were joined under EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL. The typed CSV path already had separate passing evidence, isolating the remaining failure to SQL-file replay.
behavior_before_fix.test_delta: The MariaDB mode and separate per-consumer assertions were added before the baseline run; the SQL literal writer was unchanged for that failure.

fix: The shared MySQL SQL insert literal builder emits SPACE(0) for empty Value::Text values. Native SQL-file replay checks the empty ENUM label and zero-member SET value under MariaDB EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL; a core builder test pins the same literal for ordinary text columns. SQL NULL remains represented separately.
contract: MariaDB runs EMPTY_STRING_IS_NULL alone and combined with STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, ANSI_QUOTES, and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES.
SQL-file replay and typed CSV restore are compared independently against native ENUM ordinals and bytes, SET masks and bytes, SQL NULL state, and an untouched sibling row.
The existing MySQL mode matrix still passes with independent SQL-file and CSV assertions.
A core unit test pins the SQL expression SPACE(0) for empty MySQL insert literals.
